plan.topic: Stroke in younger adults: rising rates in ages 20–54 and the BE-FAST warning signs
plan.angle: A public-service list: 'Stroke isn't just an old person's disease.' Include a slide per BE-FAST sign (Balance, Eyes, Face, Arms, Speech, Time to call emergency services), the main risk drivers (high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, smoking/drugs), and why younger adults wait too long to seek care. Quote the 'nearly doubled' figure only if the Neurology paper confirms it (the radar didn't link it). Otherwise say 'rising'.

plan.why: Evergreen life-saving content with a timely hook (2nd snapshot, CBS story). BE-FAST is exactly the kind of list people save and send to family.

package.title: Stroke Before 50: The 5 Signs That Mean Call Emergency Services Now

social.instagram_caption:
Stroke isn't just an older person's disease. Here's what to watch for at any age 🧠

CDC data: the share of US adults aged 18–44 who report having had a stroke rose 14.6% between 2011–13 and 2020–22.
About 10–15% of all strokes happen to adults aged 18–50.
High blood pressure is the biggest single driver. Most of the main risk factors can be treated or managed.
Younger people who go to the ER with dizziness or a headache are more likely to have a stroke missed. Sudden signs still count, even when you're young.

BE-FAST: Balance, Eyes, Face, Arms, Speech, Time. Just one sudden sign is enough to act. Call emergency services, note the time it started and don't drive yourself.

Save this and send it to someone you love. Knowing BE-FAST could save a life.

Did you know strokes could happen in your 20s, 30s and 40s? Tell us in the comments 👇

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation.

social.facebook_caption:
A lot of people think stroke only happens to older adults. It doesn't. About 10–15% of all strokes happen to adults aged 18–50. And CDC survey data show the share of US adults aged 18–44 who report having had a stroke rose 14.6% over about a decade.

The good news is that the biggest drivers, like high blood pressure, diabetes and smoking, can often be treated or managed. It also helps to know the warning signs. BE-FAST stands for Balance, Eyes, Face, Arms, Speech and Time. Even one sudden sign is enough to call emergency services. Note the time it started and don't drive yourself. Every minute counts.

Swipe through, then share it with someone you care about. Did you know strokes could happen this young?

#StrokeAwareness #BEFAST

carousel.title: Stroke Before 50: The 5 Signs That Mean Call Emergency Services Now

slides.headline: Stroke isn't just an old person's disease
slides.bubble: Wait… people MY age get strokes?!

slides.headline: Rise in stroke prevalence among US adults aged 18–44
slides.body: CDC survey data: the share of 18–44s who report having had a stroke rose 14.6% from 2011–13 to 2020–22. In 45–64s it rose 15.7%.

slides.headline: At least 1 in 10 strokes hits adults aged 18–50
slides.body: About 10–15% of all strokes happen to adults aged 18–50, according to a Lancet Neurology review. That's up to about 1 in 8 strokes.

slides.headline: What's driving strokes in younger adults
slides.body: These conditions damage or narrow blood vessels over years. Most can be treated or managed (CDC; drug risk: Ekker et al., Lancet Neurology, 2018).

items.label: Obesity
items.detail: Raises blood pressure and diabetes risk

slides.headline: Estimated share of strokes linked to selected risk factors
slides.body: INTERSTROKE (The Lancet, 2016): about 27,000 people in 32 countries, all ages. Other factors include blood lipids (26.8%) and diet (23.2%). Shares overlap, so they don't add up to 100%.

slides.headline: "I'm too young. It's just a migraine."
slides.body: Stroke can happen at any age. A large US ER study found stroke was missed more often in patients under 45 who came in with dizziness or headache. A sudden, severe headache with no known cause is a stroke warning sign too. If signs appear suddenly, get help.

slides.headline: BE-FAST: 5 signs + 1 rule
slides.body: Symptoms come on suddenly. Even one sign is enough to act.

items.label: B: Balance
items.detail: Sudden dizziness or loss of balance

items.label: E: Eyes
items.detail: Sudden blurred, double or lost vision

items.label: A: Arms
items.detail: One arm weak or drifts down

slides.headline: Brain cells lost each minute of stroke
slides.body: In a typical large-vessel ischaemic stroke, an estimated 1.9 million neurons die every minute without treatment (Saver, Stroke, 2006). Clot treatments work best in the first few hours.

slides.headline: Save this. Send it to someone you love.
slides.body: Sudden sign at any age? Don't wait it out. Call emergency services, note the time it started and don't drive yourself.
slides.bubble: Share it. Knowing BE-FAST could save a life.

factcheck.summary: All the main numbers and study descriptions check out against primary sources. CDC MMWR 73(20) reports stroke prevalence rising 14.6% in 18–44s and 15.7% in 45–64s between 2011–13 and 2020–22. Ekker et al. (Lancet Neurology, 2018) exists and covers adults aged 18–50; the 10–15% figure matches its abstract as I recall it, but the full text was not fetched. INTERSTROKE (Lancet, 2016) reports these population attributable risks: hypertension 47.9%, inactivity 35.8%, ApoB/ApoA1 26.8%, diet 23.2%, waist-to-hip ratio 18.6%, smoking 12.4%. Saver (Stroke, 2006) gives 1.9 million neurons lost per minute. Newman-Toker (Diagnosis, 2014) found missed stroke was more likely in patients under 45 who came in with dizziness or headache. The CDC signs page uses B.E. F.A.S.T. and lists sudden severe headache. The safety messaging is sound: call emergency services, note when symptoms started, don't drive yourself. There is no individual medical advice and no fear without a clear action. The title's promise ("5 signs") is paid off. Only small precision fixes are needed, listed below.

issues.claim: Rise in stroke among US adults aged 18–44
issues.problem: The CDC BRFSS data is self-reported lifetime stroke prevalence (ever told you had a stroke), not new cases per year. The headline could be read as a rise in new strokes.
issues.fix: Headline: "Rise in stroke prevalence among US adults aged 18–44". Body: "CDC survey data: the share of 18–44s who report having had a stroke rose 14.6% from 2011–13 to 2020–22. In 45–64s it rose 15.7%."

issues.claim: In a typical large stroke, about 1.9 million neurons die every minute
issues.problem: Saver's figure is a modelled estimate for a typical large-vessel ischaemic stroke, not a measured value for all large strokes.
issues.fix: Body: "In a typical large-vessel ischaemic stroke, an estimated 1.9 million neurons die every minute without treatment (Saver, Stroke, 2006). Clot treatments work best in the first few hours."

issues.claim: Share of strokes linked to selected risk factors
issues.problem: These are estimated population attributable risks from a case-control study. "Estimated" makes clear they are not observed shares.
issues.fix: Headline: "Estimated share of strokes linked to selected risk factors"

issues.claim: Drugs like cocaine can trigger a sudden stroke
issues.problem: The cited CDC risk-factor page (S7) does not mention cocaine or illicit drugs. The claim is well established, but only the Ekker young-stroke review (S2) supports it.
issues.fix: Keep the wording and attribute it to S2 (Ekker et al., Lancet Neurology 2018) in the source notes, not S7.

issues.claim: Signs and Symptoms of Stroke, CDC, 2024
issues.problem: The page's current date is May 19, 2026.
